newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa JSE trade delayed for 2nd consecutive day.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa JSE trade delayed for 2nd consecutive day.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said on Tuesday the start of the trading session had been delayed while a series of tests was being carried out.
"We are still testing. We will not convert to live until we are satisfied that the system is working," JSE president Roy Andersen told Reuters.
He was unsure how long the tests on the electronic Johannesburg Equities Trading system would take.
The trading system failed twice on Monday, first for three hours in the morning and again in the afternoon forcing the bourse to close 50 minutes before the official 1400 GMT closing time.

Andersen said trading had not opened at all on Tuesday morning with the market at the pre-opener stage. Earlier on Tuesday Andersen told Reuters the market would open 15 minutes later than normal due to the tests. However, an hour into the session trade had still not begun.
